skills.name: Advantages and disadvantages of vegetative propagation

note.text:
Advantages:
• The new plants are identical to the parent, so good qualities (big fruits, sweetness, resistance) are kept.
• It is faster: plants mature and bear fruit sooner than from seeds.
• It works for plants with no good seeds (banana, plantain, cassava).
• The stored food helps the new plant survive bad conditions.
Disadvantages:
• No variation: if a disease attacks, all the plants may be destroyed.
• Diseases of the parent are passed on (cassava mosaic in cuttings).
• New plants grow close to the parent: overcrowding and competition.
• Organs are bulky and heavy to store and carry, and they can rot.

worked_example.problem: A farmer grows all his {c} from cuttings of one plant. Give one advantage and one danger.
steps: Advantage: all the plants keep the good qualities of the parent and grow quickly.
Danger: they are identical, so a disease such as cassava mosaic could destroy them all, and an infected parent passes it on.
worked_example.answer: Advantage: good qualities kept; danger: no variation, diseases spread to all.

cards.idea: Vegetative propagation keeps the parent's good qualities and is faster than seeds.
example: A grafted orange tree bears fruit sooner.
Its fruits are as sweet as the parent's.

cards.idea: Its main danger is no variation: one disease can destroy every plant.
example: Diseases in the parent are passed on in cuttings.

cards.idea: New plants grow close to the parent, so they compete for light, water and minerals.
example: Suckers crowd round a banana plant.

pick.q: Why should a farmer separate banana suckers from the parent plant?
pick.y: Crowded plants compete for light, water and minerals.

pick.q: Why should cuttings be taken only from healthy plants?
pick.r: Diseases of the parent are passed on.
e: Diseased plants do not grow better.
pick.y: A sick parent gives sick offspring.
